title: feat(objectql,metadata-protocol)!: register a tenant object overlay as its own contributor layer (ADR-0029 D9)
body:
Fixes #7277

Implements ADR-0029 **D9**, ratified when PR #7087 merged (`fb5ebc5df`). The design is settled; this is the code.

## The correctness check: the resolved object does not move

D9's load-bearing property is that layering must resolve **bit for bit** to what the old splice already produced, `_provenance: 'org'` included. The pin compares two registries directly:

- left: D9 — packaged `own` + tenant `overlay`
- right: pre-D9 — the overlay body as the sole `own` (what the splice left behind)

`expect(d9.getObject(name)).toEqual(preD9.getObject(name))` (`registry-object-overlay-layer.test.ts`). **No resolved schema moved anywhere.** RV-3 below proves the pin does real work: reverting the provisioning gate turns it red, which is exactly what "the resolved object moved" looks like.

## The three things a naive implementation gets wrong — each with its own pin

**1. `getArtifactItem`'s object branch reads the OWNER contributor.** The merged body deliberately keeps `_provenance: 'org'`, so only reading the owner's layer makes `isArtifactBacked` honest. What comes back is the **code-layer baseline** (owner + its extenders); with no overlay registered it is byte-for-byte the previous answer (pinned separately). RV-1: reverting this branch to the merged read produces 6 stable reds.

**2. `provisionPrimary` / `provisionSearchCompanion` are gated on "is this a BASE layer"** (`own` or `overlay`). RV-3: reverting to `own`-only produces 2 reds — the `nameField` pin and the bit-for-bit pin.

**3. #6995's three bindings, implemented as ruled.** Same package normal; package-less sentinel **accepted** (the old throw was an artefact of the borrowed `own` slot); different package **refused loudly at the producer** with the newly minted `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / 422, and counted in `loadMetaFromDb`'s per-record `errors` at boot.

## The two items D9 left open

**Late install — measured and implemented.** When a code package registers an object a tenant row already holds, D9's recommended default is taken: the code layer becomes owner and the tenant contribution is re-classified as its overlay layer. Deliberately narrow — it fires only when the sitting owner is tenant-authored (`_provenance: 'org'`) and the incoming body is not, so two code packages claiming one name is still D3's cross-package refusal. The measurement found the same-package spelling matters too: pre-D9 it did **not** throw, it took the re-registration splice and destroyed the tenant's customization. Both spellings are pinned.

**ADR-0005's "Amended by" cross-reference** added — D9 is accepted, so that line can now assert acceptance.

## The PM's three mechanism assumptions, measured

**1. #7012's tier-3 guard — RETIRED, with a pin.** RV-5 puts the guard **back**, and exactly **one** test turns red: `a package-bound RUNTIME-authored object is retired, and its data plane closes`. That is the whole measurement. After D9 the only thing the guard still reached was its own **accepted cost** (a Studio package-workspace object staying listable-but-rowless until restart). With the predicate honest that is no longer the cheap direction — it is simply the wrong answer: nothing ships the name, the row WAS the item. The case the guard actually protected is now covered by `isArtifactBacked` itself (and `removeObjectOverlay` returns before it besides), which is why nothing else moved.

**2. Overlay removal reuses #6818's family — half true, and one correction that matters.** The layer-addressed sibling `SchemaRegistry.removeObjectOverlay(name)` is name-addressed through the same `resolveObjectKey`, so that half holds. **But it cannot live in tier 3**: tier 1 (`removeRuntimeShadow`) returns as soon as it heals the generic metadata map, so the object's overlay layer would be skipped entirely — the #6808 asymmetry, replayed one layer down. The subtraction therefore runs **ahead of the tier walk**, unconditionally for `object`.

**3. D9.6's migration cost — confirmed, and it reaches one more gate than the record names.** With the predicate honest, an overlay write to a packaged object is refused **every time** (the pin refuses three times in a row, asserting `code` AND `status`). **What D9 does not enumerate: the same predicate feeds `deleteMetaItem`'s two-tier authorization and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`**, so RESETTING such a customization is refused too — and the repository check is topology-independent, so a control-plane kernel refuses as well. Both are pinned rather than softened (a fixture encoding the old leniency would be encoding the defect). The operator hatch is the same one door, `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object`, which now has to stay open for the LIFE of the customization. Flagging this for the maintainer: it follows from D9.6's declared cost, but D9 states it only for the save side.

## File surface, declared file by file

| File | Change |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` | the contributor model: `overlay` kind, `DEFAULT_OVERLAY_PRIORITY = 150`, base selection by kind, base-layer provisioning gate, `resolveOwnerLayer`, `getPackagedObjectOwner`, `removeObjectOverlay`, orphan-overlay violation class, late install, uninstall takes the layer with its base |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` | D9.8 discriminator + D9.9 bindings (`classifyObjectContribution` / `overlayPackageMismatchError`), both hydration seams, `saveMetaItem` producer-side refusal, the delete heal's layer subtraction, **retired** `installedPackageBindingForObject` |
| `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` | D9.8's **third door**: the two metadata-service ingest seams, with a narrower rule so an owner re-registering its own body (HMR) is not mistaken for a layer |
| `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` | CROSS-SEAT — `ObjectOwnershipEnum` gains `'overlay'` plus the "loader-set, never authored" clause (D9.1, verbatim) |
| `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` | CROSS-SEAT — registers `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` under ADR-0112 |
| `content/docs/references/**` (12 files) | GENERATED, regenerated with `gen:schema` + `gen:docs`; the entire diff is the new error code (`+258 more` becomes `+259 more`) plus the ledger and object pages |
| `docs/adr/0005-*.md` | the one-line "Amended by" pointer |
| `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__registry.ts.json` | invariant rewritten from "D9 is DESIGN ONLY, do not implement" to the landed model |
| `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-protocol__src__protocol.ts.json` | protocol.ts **earns** its ADR-0029 anchor per D9 section 8 (added alongside the existing ADR-0119 entry, which is byte-unchanged) |
| `packages/objectql/src/registry-object-overlay-layer.test.ts` | new, 34 registry-level pins |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-object-overlay-layer.test.ts` | **renamed** from `protocol-delete-object-package-binding-guard.test.ts` via `git mv` (blame preserved): the guard is retired, so the file now pins the model that subsumes it — 16 cases |

Not touched: `content/docs/releases/`. Not absorbed: #6725 (the write side, `domain:engine-core`).

### CROSS-SEAT DECLARATION: two `packages/spec` files

The dispatch says to stop and report if `packages/spec` is needed. Both edits are required **verbatim** by D9.1 and D9.9, and D9.1 explicitly rejects the alternative (a parallel local union in objectql — "one vocabulary, not a parallel list", Prime Directive #8), so the card cannot be implemented as ratified without them. Measured against #6298's own admission criterion: `ObjectOwnershipEnum` has **no runtime consumer** in this repo (registry.ts imports only the type), so widening it changes **no metadata's legality** — what parsed before parses byte-for-byte after, and what was rejected stays rejected. Routing is the PM's call; splitting these out would leave the card unimplementable as designed.

## Merge with `main` (2026-08-10, head `bc4fddb27`)

`main` moved under this PR and it went `dirty`. Merged (not rebased, so the `git mv` blame on the renamed pin file survives — `git log --follow` still reaches `426cf5281`). **Exactly one conflict**, and everything else auto-merged:

- **`scripts/adr-anchors.json` — modify/delete.** #7301 sharded the ADR-anchor registry to one file per anchor and deleted the monolith, while this branch had rewritten two of its entries. Resolved as a **union, not a pick**: main's sharded layout is adopted, and both anchor bodies are ported into their shards. The port was checked rather than assumed — main's ADR-0119 sentence for `protocol.ts` was asserted byte-identical before ADR-0029 was added to it, so nothing of the other side was overwritten.
- **The 12 generated `content/docs/references/**` files** — took main's side wholesale, then re-ran `gen:schema` + `gen:docs`. No hand-merging. The regenerated tree differs from `main` by exactly the same 12 files / +70 -67 as before the merge (the new error code plus the ledger and object pages); `data-engine.mdx` and `app.mdx` dropped out of the diff, confirming they were main's own updates arriving rather than drift here.
- `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` — no concurrent registration; the diff against `main` is still exactly the one added line.

**Nothing incoming touched D9's model.** `main`'s #7260 widened the RECORD-ownership enum to `user | business_unit | org | none` — a different enum from the CONTRIBUTION kind (`own | extend | overlay`) — and both sides' edits to that shared doc block survived intact (the NOTE now reads `own | extend | overlay` next to the four record tiers). `main`'s only change to `registry.ts` was comment-only, inside `applySystemFields`. `registerObject`, `resolveObject`, `getArtifactItem`, both hydration seams and the delete heal were untouched by `main`, and every D9 marker was re-grepped in the merged tree. **No pin moved**: both pin files are byte-identical to `426cf5281` and still 34 + 16 green.

Re-run on the merged tree: `objectql` 168 files / 2975 tests, `metadata-protocol` 67 / 862 (the +1 each is main's own new tests arriving), breadth spot check `runtime` 119/1870 and `rest` 77/1228 — all green. Gates re-run and exit 0: `check:adr-anchors`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:nul-bytes`, and spec-side `check:generated`, `check:docs`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`.

## Reverse verification: direction decided before each run

Every probe reverts to **this PR's own base**, and `dist` is rebuilt before reading any result.

| Probe | Predicted | Measured | Reading |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **RV-1** `getArtifactItem` back to the merged body (D9.6) | 5 red | **6 stable red** + 1 unstable | One missed prediction: the late-install pin **also** asserts `getArtifactItem` is honest — cause identified. The unstable one (`a package-bound RUNTIME-authored object is retired`) is GREEN at `--maxWorkers=1` and green in isolation under the same probe, so it is an ordering artefact of the probe run and is **not counted as evidence** |
| **RV-2** base selection back to `own` (D9.2) | 6-8 red | **11 red** | Under-predicted. The bit-for-bit pin, the provenance pin, the overlay-is-not-an-extender counter-example, the priority-140 attack, layer replacement and both late-install cases all go red |
| **RV-3** provisioning gate back to `own` only | **exactly 1 red** | **2 red** | Missed one, and it is the valuable one: **the bit-for-bit pin goes red too**. Skipping title provisioning on the overlay layer MOVES the resolved schema — precisely what D9 forbids |
| **RV-4** both hydration seams back to `'own'` (D9.8) | ~9 red, all in the e2e file | **exactly 9 red, 0 in the registry unit file** | Hit. The registry unit file registers `'overlay'` directly and never crosses a seam, so it is immune to this probe — as predicted |
| **RV-5** #7012's guard put **back** | **exactly 1 red** (its own accepted cost) | **exactly 1 red** | Hit. This is the measured basis for retiring it |

**Green in BOTH directions — reported as guards, not as evidence**: `assertSingleOwnerPerObject` still counts exactly one owner on an overlaid object (D9.5 is literally unchanged); a second cross-package owner is still refused; with no overlay the artifact item still carries its extenders; a tenant re-writing its own runtime object stays a single `own`; package-less and non-installed-binding objects are still retired; a non-object type is untouched by the mismatch rule.

**Unmeasured**: none. The one unstable RV-1 red is reported above as unstable rather than counted as passed.

## Tests and gates (local, on `426cf5281` before the merge)

```
@objectstack/objectql          168 files / 2974 tests  passed
@objectstack/metadata-protocol  67 files /  861 tests  passed
@objectstack/metadata           30 files /  593 tests  passed
@objectstack/runtime           118 files / 1837 tests  passed
@objectstack/rest               76 files / 1219 tests  passed
@objectstack/plugin-security    43 files /  878 tests  passed
@objectstack/cli               105 files / 1139 tests  passed
```

The suites that actually **exercise the changed path** are `objectql` (registry pins plus protocol end-to-end over a real `SchemaRegistry`) and `metadata-protocol`. The other five are the consumption-radius sweep: all green, but they barely touch the changed path, and that is stated rather than counted as evidence.

`plugin-security` first reported 4 files failing to LOAD — the fresh-worktree unbuilt-dependency false red (AGENTS.md section 9); after `pnpm --filter 'PKG^...' build` it is 43/43 green.

Gates run locally, all exit 0: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:adr-anchors`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:doc-authoring`, and on the spec package `check:generated`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:api-surface`, `check:exported-any`, `check:dual-source-exports`, `check:skill-examples`, `check:react-blocks`. ESLint is clean on every changed file.

Note: a whole-repo `pnpm lint` in this container reports `Parsing error: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` (291 KB, **untouched by this PR**) — a container Node stack limit, not this change. CI's ESLint job is the authority.
